title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 45
content:
Latest tech news from the Wikimedia technical community. Please tell other users about these changes. Not all changes will affect you. Translations are available.

Weekly highlight

  • Many Wikimedia tools were taken offline last week because of a security vulnerability in PHP. This affected many websites worldwide. Toolforge and Cloud VPS have been back up since October 22. Many important tools have been gradually restored. Some tools need the respective volunteer maintainers to restart them. Others still need to upgrade to a patched PHP version. Some tools were using older versions of PHP which are not supported by the recent security patches. They will require maintainers to upgrade to a more recent version. This might require additional effort. You can follow the work on Wikitech.

title: Beyond Edit-a-Thons: Building Sustainable Pathways for Queer Wikimedia Contributors
content:
What happens after the event ends? Reflections from Queering Wiki 2026 on strengthening Wikimedia communities and sustaining participation.

Wikimedia communities know how to bring people into the room. Edit-a-thons, workshops, and campaigns introduce people to free knowledge, help them develop skills, and create opportunities to connect with others. But what happens when the event ends?

Some participants may want to continue contributing but need guidance, resources, or opportunities to collaborate. Others may be ready to take on new responsibilities but not know where to begin. Without pathways to continued participation, the momentum created by an event can be difficult to sustain.

This question shaped my presentation, “Beyond Edit-a-Thons: Building Sustainable Pathways for Queer Wikimedia Contributors,” at the Queering Wiki Conference 2026 in Montréal, Canada. Drawing on the work of the EduWiki Hub, I explored how mentorship, peer learning, shared resources, and community support can contribute to more sustainable participation.

An event can introduce someone to Wikimedia, but attendance alone does not tell us whether they feel connected, supported, or able to continue contributing.
snippet: What happens after the event ends? Reflections from Queering Wiki 2026 on strengthening Wikimedia communities and sustaining participation.
creator: Bukola James

title: The Virtual Room: How Volunteers Brought Wikimania Paris to the World
content:
From 22 to 25 July 2026, Wikimania Paris featured a room that nobody could physically walk into.

The Virtual Room was a dedicated digital space built exclusively for online attendees, complete with its own dedicated programming and unique content unavailable anywhere else at the venue.

As a member of the Core Organising Team (COT), co-lead of the Technical Committee, and the primary lead for the Virtual Room, I had a front-row seat to this experiment. This is the story of how a small, dedicated group of volunteers brought a digital-first stage to life.

One of our core commitments on the COT for Wikimania 2026 was to meaningfully engage the global remote audience, not just broadcast physical sessions at them. The Technical Committee pitched several ideas to bridge the hybrid gap, and the Virtual Room was our boldest initiative.

Unlike standard track rooms, the Virtual Room had no physical space where people sat and watched. It existed entirely online, streamed through the live section of Eventyay and broadcast on the Wikimedia Foundation’s YouTube channel.
snippet: From 22 to 25 July 2026, Wikimania Paris featured a room that nobody could physically walk into.
creator: Zakaria Baou

title: How we measure contributions and recognise the most active contributors to Ukrainian Wikimedia sister projects
content:
Every year, Wikimedia Ukraine recognises some of the most active contributors to Ukrainian-language Wikimedia sister projects. To do this fairly, we look beyond simple edit counts: different projects involve very different types of work, so the indicators and tools we use depend on the nature of each project. This year, while determining winners for 2025, we also experimented with a new challenge — measuring contributions specifically to the Ukrainian-language layer of Wikidata.

For Ukraine, developing these projects has an additional significance. In the context of Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine, preserving, expanding and making Ukrainian-language knowledge accessible online is also part of strengthening the visibility and resilience of Ukrainian culture, history and language in the global information space.

We are happy to present the 2025 recipients:

🥇 Albedo
🥈 Bicolino34
🥉 Almanbet Janışev

🔗 Wikidata — contributions to Ukrainian-language content

title: Celebrating Community, Progress and Achievements at the Wikimedia Uganda Annual General Meeting 2026
content:
The Wikimedia Community User Group Uganda (WCUGU) held its Annual General Meeting (AGM) on Saturday, 5 September 2026, at Hotel Elianah, bringing together 77 participants, including volunteers, Board members, staff and partners. The AGM provided an opportunity for members to reflect on WCUGU’s work, discuss organisational development, share experiences and feedback, review financial performance, and identify priorities for the coming period, guided by four strategic objectives.

The AGM was attended by 77 participants, including Wikimedia volunteers, Board members, staff, partners and other stakeholders. Their participation created an opportunity to share experiences and perspectives on WCUGU’s development, strengthening community engagement. Media engagement also increased visibility, with Otage Stephen from Daily Monitor attending and the AGM shared on its social media platforms. The 7 September 2026 Daily Monitor edition also documented progress towards Runyankole Wikipedia going live. Links: Daily Monitor

title: How has Q3 looked in the culture and heritage world?
content:
Between July and September 2026, the This Month in GLAM reports covered projects on six continents. Read together, they keep coming back to four ideas: the value of small institutions, the languages that other platforms overlook, the technical plumbing that holds it all up, and the community of people doing the work.

Much of the best work this quarter came from modest institutions. The Czartoryski Library in Kraków (Poland) completed two years of its Wikimedian in Residence programme, releasing 354 reproductions, including a pocket map of Paris timed for Wikimania. Also in Poland, the Museum of Photography (MuFo) added more than 130 historical photographs, and two university libraries, in Wrocław and Toruń, are preparing their own residents.

In Italy, Note condivise brings four institutions together: Teatro Regio di Torino, the Associazione Musicale Estense in Modena, and the Boccherini and Scarlatti conservatories. Santa Cecilia in Rome, also in Italy, continues digitising scores and librettos. In Tunisia, a one-month residency at the National Documentation Center showed how much a short, focused engagement can open up.

title: A Journey Through Museums, Memories, and Open Knowledge
content:
My name is Elicefa, and i come from Kendal, a regency in Central Java, Indonesia. My involvement in the Wikimedia movement is closely connected to communities, local knowledge, and efforts to document cultural heritage so that more people can access it.

Attending the ESEAP Conference 2026 in Taiwan was a valuable experience. There was always something new to learn from the people I met and the activities I joined. I had the opportunity to meet Wikimedians from different backgrounds, listen to their experiences, and see how contributions from different communities are connected through the wider Wikimedia movement.

One of the most memorable activities was the cultural crawl, which included a visit to the Takao Railway Museum in Kaohsiung. This visit reminded me of the Ambarawa Railway Museum in Central Java, Indonesia.

title: Whose Stories Get Remembered? WikiGap Nigeria 2026 Takes Another Step Towards Closing the Gender Gap
content:
Think of a woman whose work has changed her community, shaped an industry, influenced public life or opened doors for others. How much of her story can someone discover with a simple search online? How much of what she has accomplished has been documented, properly sourced and made accessible to the next person looking for her name?

For many women, the answer is not enough.

This is one of the reasons WikiGap matters. Across Wikipedia and other open knowledge platforms, the stories of women remain unevenly represented. Some are difficult to find; others have received little attention beyond their immediate communities. Their contributions may be known to the people whose lives they have touched, yet remain largely absent from the knowledge the rest of the world can access.

In Nigeria, WikiGap is an opportunity to do something about that absence. It brings people together to document women’s lives and achievements, encourage more women to participate in open knowledge, and create space for conversations about who gets represented in the digital world.

title: What’s new in The Wikipedia Library? (July – September 2026)
content:
Over the past three months, we secured access to two new resources for eligible editors: The Chronicle of Higher Education and Datawrapper. We also raised awareness of the library through community convenings across the globe.

The Chronicle of Higher Education, a leading resource for independent journalism, career development, and academic analysis, made 100 subscriptions available for Wikipedia Library users (apply here). Thanks to an introduction by Doc James, Datawrapper is offering 100 free accounts for editors to create charts, maps, and tables for Wikimedia projects (apply here).

Adam Matthew Digital is transitioning to the Library Bundle, granting instant access to all eligible editors. Springer Nature has renewed access through the Library Bundle and E-Yearbook has also been renewed for another year (apply here).

title: Beyond Wikipedia: IMDUG at IndiaFOSS 2026
content:
At IndiaFOSS 2026, FOSS United’s annual conference (26–27 September 2026, NIMHANS Convention Centre, Bengaluru), the booth of the Indic MediaWiki Developers User Group (IMDUG) was a space for curiosity, conversations, and discovering the world of Wikimedia. 300 visitors stopped by to learn more about Wikimedia and its projects. Almost everyone had heard of Wikipedia, and many relied on it to find information online. But fewer knew about the wider ecosystem of Wikimedia projects, the open-source software behind them, or the many ways they could contribute to building free knowledge.

The booth saw 35 sign-ups from visitors who want to start contributing and loads of great conversations, giving us an opportunity to connect with the FOSS community and introduce more people to the Wikimedia movement.

For many visitors, our conversations began with a simple question: Have you ever wondered what makes Wikipedia possible?

title: Celebrating 14 Years of Wikidata: Learning, Editing and Growing the Community at Kenya National Library Service Buruburu
content:
At KNLS Buruburu Library, Wikidata’s 14th birthday brought together learning, conversations about knowledge gaps, a birthday cake and an unexpected new contributor.

On 24 October 2026, Kenya National Library Service Buruburu Library in Nairobi, Kenya, hosted a celebration of Wikidata’s 14th birthday. The event brought together participants interested in open knowledge, information sharing and contributing to Wikimedia projects.

For me, the day was more than a birthday celebration. As the trainer, I had an opportunity to introduce participants to Wikidata, explain how they could contribute, and explore with them how we can work together to improve the representation of Kenyan and African knowledge online.

The event also brought a lovely surprise: our photographer, who had come to document the celebration, ended up joining the Wikidata team herself!

We began the day with an icebreaker facilitated by Yusuf. The activity encouraged participants to interact, get to know one another and settle into the day’s programme.
snippet: At KNLS Buruburu Library, Wikidata’s 14th birthday brought together learning, conversations about knowledge gaps, a birthday cake and an unexpected new contributor.
